## Design

### 2026-10-11 – ![Downstream Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/32e7de20d9229e0968c1e5609ce636575d9d769453a25f858d37fec3ee8fd2ee.png)

**3h**

![Downstream Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/32e7de20d9229e0968c1e5609ce636575d9d769453a25f858d37fec3ee8fd2ee.png)
This was my first time ever designing a PCB, so it was a very slow process at first. I learned the basics from a few tutorials and began working on it with basically no plan. First, I completed the upstream (It says downstream, but I mixed the two up), which is basically the male USB that plugs into a device.

![BugFixing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/cf836de890566e4be4bf2a70e09fded6d298af6f34ed44a0a374a3980dd0fe95.png)
I then encountered a couple of errors, which I had to do even more research on in order to fix. It was actually quite simple, though, and I managed to fix all of those up.

![FullSchematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/6c4226de193bc20a4d5f102ce1ccda94445501288a0da9280f9f8fb6c37dcc1c.png)
I proceeded to work on the rest of the schematic- the downstream parts where you can plug in two USB-A and 2 USB C devices. This was the harder part of the project, but again, by following the tutorial on Hack Club and with the help of others, I finished the whole thing.

### 2026-10-11 – ![Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/fe5ba12d1c41bc6a5515dfc6664d3d350b564b3afcc3bfe40a8d2885be269648.png)

**6h**

![Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/fe5ba12d1c41bc6a5515dfc6664d3d350b564b3afcc3bfe40a8d2885be269648.png)
In order to turn the schematic into a PCB design, I needed to find physical components that correspond to the design that I could use. Again, I don't know anything about components so I looked the parts up and decided to go with the simplest ones I could find that worked for me.

![RawPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/b90e06fc6fed10e27c1ebb991d5cdda03deadabbdb00f1ece3e75cb4a6ebc43f.png)
Then I imported the schematic into the PCB design software, which is what the picture above shows. Turns out, this would take even longer than the schematic since the connections can't overlap each other, which I didn't know.

![Capacitators and Resistors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/9c9d0398ec6e8b7afec45f3f6d4569300d18d298e2904e4729daa015b60acb59.png)
I started off with something simple: the resistors and capacitors that had few connections. I tweaked them around for a bit, and this is when I realized that the connections can't overlap.

![Rearranged PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/6e91f0791f4c9701cab7a39394cdb053fe7e02958758c47dff28350ca20e08b4.png)
So, I completely started over and began wiring everything from scratch. This proved to be much more time-consuming and difficult. I kept having to change things up and tweak things because the wires would block each other and get in the way. This was definitely the longest part of the project.

![Errors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5de2e7b33969534fdd18700f1dbbfebd46f85316bab3a8da780baef1df3c62cb.png)
Just when I thought I was done, I was hit with 25 error messages. Honestly, I wanted to quit because I'd already been working on it for so long, but I powered through and fixed all of them one by one, which took forever. It was anything from unconnected items to hole clearance violations.

![FinalPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/dc13f089319dda2284e4260c47972a1655bba21f11a5fbc305b59c3b3bbfb2b5.png)
Finally, once that was done, I added a back copper layer that connected all of my ground pins and made the final finishing touches.

### 2026-10-25 – The coding took even longer than designing the actual PCB, as I am pretty new to it and I decided to add a lot of features.

**8h**

The coding took even longer than designing the actual PCB, as I am pretty new to it and I decided to add a lot of features.

First, I imported all of the necessary things from the internet for MIDI stuff.
![import](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/bded24973468f9d4f33d5649f72c8c6171a52c1d3d53fc64e5eb172e6d9897b3.png)

This part tells the computer to treat the Raspberry Pi as a MIDI device.
![keysanddrums](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/ce5e67547724356289ec1550f2de863e12758fe56cbf2ba37f4685daae56ca83.png)

I added modes where you can switch between drums and notes. The initial setting starts as notes, and the base note is 48 or C3. The drums are channel 10 or 9 on the PCB since it starts at 0.
![initialnote](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/2930de2ae68d62891886d2cac65d5822d1e2adc0b16b53f55921dde5d7c9109f.png)

This is the code to switch the modes. It basically converts the signal from the switch on the PCB and translates that to either melody or drums based on the position.
![modeswitch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/68e3822ec51f55a83c7af9929b3218277e959da72a66c28aeea8a37bbe3aa94a.png)

In a loop that repeats 100 times per second so there's no delay, it first checks for the mode. It takes the output and prints it.
![drumormelody](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/e90049943dd30596fec01a53c23d249e057344bb2c4ca18c19a14e5b87ac7eda.png)

This is a system to make sure that the notes don't go too high or too low. It checks the current number and whether it wants to go up or down. If it exceeds the limits, it doesn't do it.
![octaveboundary](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/0a7faf27d1adf79bc9a5207d624aea6b93b6d1d8998fb55e865c79356f6ee615.png)

This part checks if a key is pressed down or not, and if it is, it plays that note.
![playkey](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/638c2967d8f40409bbadb7a42bcbb49f668579ccfe45bb145fb7e02feeeb851c.png)

This is the volume slider, and I implemented a system where it takes in the movement, and if it's too small, it ignores it.
![volume](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/83517a88c569c64f541178a9769ff00f83109366c7084e8b863598eefb995824.png)
